## Abstract

This session introduces **classical environmental policy instruments** and how their
effectiveness can be evaluated from an economic perspective.

## 📊 Data for the Kaya decomposition

The decomposition of Germany's and China's CO₂ emissions uses the openly available
[CO₂ dataset of Our World in Data](https://github.com/owid/co2-data).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The computations behind the decomposition (slide 7)

**The setup.** The Kaya identity writes emissions as a product of four terms, and we want to
know how much of the change between 1990 and 2022 goes to each term. Changing one term at a
time does not work well here: if the other terms stay at their 1990 values, the pieces do not
add up to the total change, and if we change them in sequence, the result depends on the
order. The slide therefore uses the additive **log-mean Divisia index** (LMDI).

For Germany, the numbers are as follows (GDP in international dollars, ratio = 2022/1990):

| Term                        |      1990 |    2022 |     Ratio |  ln(ratio) | Effect (Mt) |
|:----------------------------|----------:|--------:|----------:|-----------:|------------:|
| Population (million)        |      79.7 |    84.1 |     1.055 |      0.053 |         +45 |
| GDP per person              |    25,287 |  46,495 |     1.839 |      0.609 |        +517 |
| Energy per GDP (kWh/dollar) |      2.08 |    0.87 |     0.420 |     −0.868 |        −737 |
| CO₂ per energy (kg/kWh)     |     0.252 |   0.197 |     0.782 |     −0.246 |        −209 |
| **CO₂ (Mt)**                | **1,055** | **671** | **0.637** | **−0.452** |    **−383** |

**Step 1: logarithms.** The logarithm turns a product into a sum, so the log changes of the
four terms add up exactly to the log change in emissions:
$0.053 + 0.609 - 0.868 - 0.246 = -0.452$.

**Step 2: back to Mt.** To turn log changes into Mt CO₂, we multiply them by the
**logarithmic mean** of emissions in the two years:

$$
L = \frac{\mathcal{E}^{2022} - \mathcal{E}^{1990}}{\ln \mathcal{E}^{2022} - \ln \mathcal{E}^{1990}}
= \frac{671.5 - 1{,}054.8}{\ln 671.5 - \ln 1{,}054.8} = 848.8
$$

By construction, $848.8 \cdot (-0.4516) = -383.3$ Mt, the total change.

**Step 3: the effects.** Each term gets the same treatment. For GDP per person,
$848.8 \cdot 0.609 = +517$ Mt. These are the bars on the slide. They sum to the total change
without a residual; the $-384$ you get from the rounded values in the table is only a rounding
difference.

**What the effects do not tell you.** They are accounting contributions, not causes. The
$-737$ Mt does not say what emissions would have been with a constant energy intensity, because
the terms also affect each other (see the caution on slide 5). And since the formula uses
logarithms, all values must be positive.

The method is explained in @ang2005, a short practical guide. @ang2015 discusses which LMDI
variant to use for which purpose.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Decompose your own country

The R script `policy_02_figures.R` in the
[`analysis/` folder of the course repository](https://github.com/graebnerc/EcolEcon26/tree/main/analysis)
prints this table. Put your country into `countries` and run it: which Kaya term is your
country's story? The
[README](https://github.com/graebnerc/EcolEcon26/blob/main/analysis/README.md#session-7a-policy-instruments)
explains how.
:::
